column1: # Batman: Arkham City (Switch, update 1.0.2 = v131072; the base NSP is a 13 MB stub). Brought up on the Mac.
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; the bring-up and its measurements are in this profile's README.md
# Rocksteady's Unreal Engine 3 (package version 864, licensee 0x80e3) on NVN, with Wwise for the sound, CRI Sofdec for the movies and Scaleform for the menus. SDK 14.3.0.
# The port compiles its NVN programs at load time: the containers (BMSG GlobalShaderCache-Switch.bin, the .xxx packages) hold the code areas but no control section to key
# them with, so the profile's shaders are run-time dumps of this build (DM_NVN_SHDUMP, shdump/) — see README.md, Shaders.
# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB (profile_guess.py: a 3328 MB heap region); the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled
# is false as on Horizon. The first boot ran to frame 900 at this block with the host heap unmoved (README.md, What it needs)
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 (the host logged "depth mode: near=0, vertex shaders use the main0_z entry" at boot)

column1: # The game asks for present interval 2 (30 fps, as on the Switch). present_interval display presents every vsync whatever the game asks for. The engine has no frame limit of its own:
# uncapped (DM_PRESENT_HZ=0 DM_FPS_TARGET=0) this build runs 632-746 fps and holds whatever the present tick gives (60.0 at 60 Hz), so present_paced tells the host 120 needs no limiter write.
# an engine with no frame limit of its own, stepping by the time that passed: presenting at the target is all it needs (fps_high accepts 120 with no limiter to write)
